checkResults.scenario: QA_Platform_Create draft event group as the seed for an RFP-only project
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200. EventGroups::CreateService persists one EventGroup row with status=draft (enum 2) and one EventGroupLineItem with status=draft, serial_number=1 and meta_data.quantity={value:10,unitSymbol:'Nos'}; response is EventGroup::ShowSerializer.
steps: 1. Authenticate as a purchaser of the workspace that owns {{productUuid}}.
2. POST /event_groups with status draft, a title and exactly one line item.
3. Assert HTTP 200 and that the response carries an event_group uuid plus one event_group_line_item id.
4. GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} and confirm status is draft with no trade_requests yet.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated purchaser with EventGroupPolicy#create? allowed in the workspace; {{productUuid}} and {{productQualityUuid}} resolve to an active Product / ProductQuality in the caller's company.

checkResults.scenario: [Technical / RFP only] A fresh single-stage draft activates
checkResults.expectedResult: 200; the event group is active with one live stage. Status active; the stage appears in `stages`; a vendor can bid on it.
steps: 1. `PATCH` with `status: "active"` and the stage uuid in `draft_trade_request_uuids`.
checkResults.preconditions: A draft event group with one draft stage that has a bidding-time schedule.

checkResults.scenario: [Technical / RFP only] Activation must never answer with an untyped 500
checkResults.expectedResult: Either 200, or a `render_error_json` failure with a `{code, message}`. Fail if the body is `{"status":500,"error":…}` with no code. Attach the payload to the failure — the payload is what makes the report actionable. The three ranked causes are a `lock_transaction` double-render at `event_groups_controller.rb:74`, `set_customized_audiences` (`trade_controller_helper.rb:687-729`), and `TradeSchedule.change_auction_time(nil)` in `publish_auction`; the third cannot explain the draft-status 500, so an exception class from Sentry is what distinguishes them.
steps: 2. Capture the full response body and the request payload.
checkResults.preconditions: Any valid draft event group and stage.

checkResults.scenario: [Technical / RFP only] Activation of a stage with no bidding-time schedule fails cleanly
checkResults.expectedResult: A `{code, message}` refusal about the schedule. Not a bare 500. This is the regression guard's narrowest form.
checkResults.preconditions: A draft stage whose bidding-time `TradeSchedule` is absent.
checkResults.weakReason: This case documents a refusal, but the request sent is the generic valid payload for PATCH /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} — the change it describes (PATCH to activate.) is not in it. So all this run can honestly check is that the server answered without an untyped 500. Write the perturbation into PERTURBATIONS in scripts/import-written-api-cases.mjs and the case asserts the refusal itself.

checkResults.scenario: QA_Platform_Config sent as a string instead of an object must not crash create
